rubric: The chart is an honest, readable form for a 12-week trend: a baseline that starts at zero or is clearly marked, labelled units, and no distorted scale.
The chart is labelled directly or with a minimal axis: few gridlines, no heavy borders, no legend for a single series, and the title says what is shown.
Table numbers are right-aligned with consistent decimals and currency formatting, and the columns are easy to scan.
Colour is restrained: one main colour for the data, with any highlight used on purpose rather than for decoration.
Chart and table form one coherent page with clear hierarchy, and nothing is clipped or overflowing.

result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): A fits the whole report on one screen: all 6 table rows are visible and the colours are a restrained brown. Its main flaws are that the bars fill only the left half of the plot area and the Units Sold column is centred instead of right-aligned. B's chart uses the space well, and its numbers are right-aligned, but the table is cut off after 3 rows, so it doesn't meet the one-screen requirement, and its $0 gridline sits slightly off the axis. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A has the cleaner chart, with a zero baseline, light gridlines and bars that fill the width. But its table is cut off after three rows, so the page fails its main job as a one-screen screenshot. B shows all six products and has a clearer header hierarchy. Its weaknesses are a chart that fills only the left half of its panel with tiny labels, and a units column that is centred instead of right-aligned.
